frequency_question: How often do proposed joint resolutions of disapproval successfully pass both chambers of Congress and survive or override a presidential veto within the statutory window for bilateral nuclear cooperation or equivalent major foreign policy compacts?
membership_rule: Includes formal 123 agreements transmitted to Congress under the Atomic Energy Act where a joint resolution of disapproval was introduced and brought to a vote; excludes informal notifications, non-binding resolutions, or agreements withdrawn before statutory deadlines.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named historical instances of major legislative disapproval challenges against executive foreign policy/nuclear pacts in the modern era; zero instances of a successful veto-proof joint resolution blocking such an agreement.
known_gaps: Excludes minor civilian nuclear cooperation agreements that did not reach floor votes for disapproval.
skeleton: Total formal disapproval resolution attempts on major Middle Eastern nuclear/arms agreements divided by successful overrides
multiplier: 0 successful overrides / 3 major attempted congressional blocks
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing congressional review of 123 agreements (Atomic Energy Act) remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
